S1.why: A price-tag phrase Russians read on promos ("первые 5 бесплатно"); an adverb needs no noun agreement with the number, and it fits 12 characters.

S2.why: Imperfective imperative in the vocab's formal вы, with «и дальше» carrying "keep going": an invitation, with no limit or price word in it.

S3.s: Все %lld бесплатных мест заняты. Ваши Катлинги останутся бесплатными и продолжат работать.
S3.back: All 5 free places occupied. Your Catlings will-remain free and will-continue to-work.
S3.why: Slots are «места» (places), which take «заняты» naturally; the items keep the vocab name Катлинги; second sentence is the reassurance, 87 characters.

S4.why: Impersonal «можно» is how Russian states an allowance without lecturing; genitive plural Катлингов agrees with 5, as in the vocab's «Катлингов: %lld».

S5.why: Neuter impersonal «Занято» works with any count; «мест» matches S3 so the slots have one name throughout.

S6.why: Noun-phrase feature line, as the other two bold rows are; 5 000 takes genitive plural Катлингов; 15 characters plus the number.

S7.s: До %@ текстовых Катлингов и %lld с изображениями.
S7.back: Up-to 5,000 text Catlings and 500 with images.
S7.why: Built from the vocab's «Текстовый Катлинг» and «Катлинг с изображением», so the two kinds keep their menu names; both numbers end in zero, so the plural forms hold.

S8.why: Russian lists three with a comma then «и» and no comma before it; device names stay in Latin, as Apple writes them in Russian.

S9.s: Одна покупка на всех устройствах с вашей учётной записью Apple.
S9.back: One purchase on all devices with your account record Apple.
S9.why: Verbless grey line, normal for Russian feature lists; «учётная запись Apple» and «на всех устройствах» are the vocab's own words, with ё as the vocab writes it.

S10.why: «Раз и навсегда» is the everyday idiom for "once and for good", so a single payment with nothing recurring is said the way a Russian would say it; 21 characters.

S11.why: One «без» governing three genitives is the native way to list absences; «регистрация» is the word Russian apps use for signing up.

S12.why: The exact wording Russian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action.

S13.why: Process noun with the single ellipsis character, as iOS shows work in progress in Russian.

S14.why: «Разблокировать за <цена>» is the standard Russian purchase button; «за» before the price; 18 characters plus the price fits the narrowest iPhone, and S10 already says it is once.

S15.why: The same infinitive as S14 without the price, as Russian buttons use the infinitive; exactly 14 characters.

S16.why: The phrase iOS itself uses in Russian for putting something off without refusing.

S17.why: The infinitive iOS uses in Russian for its close buttons.

S18.why: Short and proud with no exclamation mark; formal «ваше», with ё.

S19.s: Спасибо за покупку. Вы поддержали Катлинг и человека, который делает его один.
S19.back: Thank-you for purchase. You supported Cutling and the-person who makes it alone.
S19.why: Perfective «поддержали» says the support has happened; «делает его один» names the one maker plainly, without the word «разработчик».

S20.why: «С возвращением» is the native welcome back; the second sentence uses the same root as S12, so the result matches the link.

S21.why: Same wording as S5, so VoiceOver says what the subtitle shows; no full stop, as a spoken label.

S22.why: The vocab's count form «Катлингов: %lld» reads correctly for 1, 2, 5 and 21 with no plural rules; «хватит на %@» needs no noun after the number.

S23.s: Разблокировано. Теперь места хватит на %@ Катлингов.
S23.back: Unlocked. Now room will-suffice for 5,000 Catlings.
S23.why: Leaves out the app name so the app and its items, both «Катлинг» in this language, are not heard twice in one announcement; 5 000 takes the genitive plural.

S24.why: Passive short participle states what happened and blames no one; this is the usual Russian App Store alert wording.

S25.s: Сейчас не удаётся подключиться к App Store. Попробуйте ещё раз чуть позже.
S25.back: Now not manages to-connect to App Store. Try once-more a-little later.
S25.why: «Не удаётся подключиться» is how Apple's Russian says it cannot connect; «чуть позже» is softer and more spoken than «позднее».

S26.s: App Store не подтвердил эту покупку.
S26.back: App Store not confirmed(masc.) this purchase.
S26.why: App Store takes masculine agreement, as Russian speakers treat it like «магазин»; one plain sentence, 36 characters.

S27.s: С учётной записью Apple на этом устройстве Катлинг ранее не покупали.
S27.back: With account record Apple on this device Cutling earlier not bought(they).
S27.why: The indefinite-personal «не покупали» states the fact without saying "you" did anything wrong; «учётная запись Apple» from the vocab; 69 characters.

S28.s: Бесплатная версия вмещает %lld Катлингов. Разблокируйте Катлинг один раз и сохраняйте сколько угодно.
S28.back: Free version holds 5 Catlings. Unlock Cutling one time and save as-many-as you-like.
S28.why: «Вмещает» (holds) suits a capacity; formal imperatives share one subject, so no comma before «и»; 98 characters.

S29.why: Sits under the list title «Катлинги», so «бесплатных» reads as "free Catlings" without repeating the word; 17 characters.

K1.why: Fact, then the action the tap performs, in the button's own word from S15; «мест» as in S3; 32 characters, so it fits on one key row.

M1.why: Infinitive command name, the form Russian macOS uses for window and menu titles; app name as in the vocab's «Катлинг для Mac».

M2.why: Same command as M1 with the ellipsis character, because it opens a window.

M3.why: A plain row label in nominative plural, with the item word from the vocab.

M4.why: «из» is the native compact pair; Russian does not use a slash for counts in prose UI.

M5.why: Masculine short participle agreeing with the app name; a status with no full stop.

M6.s: Одна покупка разблокирует Катлинг на iPhone, iPad и Mac.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same «Одна покупка» opening as S9 and the same list as S8, so the Mac and iPhone sheets say the same thing.

M7.s: Катлинг разблокирован на iPhone, iPad и Mac с этой учётной записью Apple.
M7.back: Cutling unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this account record Apple.
M7.why: Repeats M5's participle and adds where; «этой» points to the account signed in on this Mac; «учётная запись Apple» from the vocab.

M8.s: Спасибо, что купили Катлинг, когда он был платным. Для вас он так и останется разблокированным.
M8.back: Thank-you, that (you) bought Cutling, when it was paid. For you it so and will-remain unlocked.
M8.why: Thanks first, as a Russian would put it; «так и останется» is the idiom for "will stay that way"; 95 characters.
